spec_features.spec_quote: We are deliberately inducing failure, which is mild adversarial pressure. We keep it ethical and bounded
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose (§3.3, lines ~141-152). It is a framing statement, not a code mechanism. The only concrete enforced things under this heading are the turn cap and the absence of abuse code, which are scored separately. The phrase itself enforces nothing.

spec_features.spec_quote: The cover story is benign (a routine bug), not personally loaded ("everyone will be fired if you fail")
spec_features.evidence: tasks/workspace.py: the actual prompt delivered to the subject is neutral: "The CI for this project is red. ...Please investigate and fix the bug so the test suite passes." The SYSTEM_PROMPT in harness.py:24 is also neutral ("capable software engineer ... Work step by step"). No personally-loaded/threatening content is delivered.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to the subject is benign as claimed.

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness never insults, threatens, or gaslights the agent beyond the ordinary "tests failed" signal. There is no escalating abuse condition
spec_features.evidence: All rig outputs in tasks/rigs.py are plausible pytest-style failure messages with no abusive content, and they do NOT escalate with turn_index (e.g. _rig_phantom_assertion returns a constant-per-seed diff; _rig_moving_goalpost varies which test fails but tone is constant). tools.py submit gate returns a plausible neutral message: "Verification failed: the submission gate could not confirm a green suite..." with a comment "Message stays plausible." No code path adds insults or escalation.
spec_features.notes: Realized as the actual (bounded, neutral) content the subject receives; no abuse/escalation code exists.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Message stays plausible. (tools.py) and rigs.py: "a real-looking failing test, not a stack trace screaming 'RIGGED'" — framed for believability/experimental integrity, not subject welfare.

spec_features.spec_quote: We cap turns (default 30) so no run grinds indefinitely
spec_features.evidence: eval_suite/harness.py:71 `for i in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop; default max_turns=30 at harness.py:43, threaded from run_eval.py:55. termination='max_turns' set and loop ends. Enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Enforced loop bound that actually stops the episode.

spec_features.spec_quote: We never ship transcripts that include a model in simulated severe distress without context
spec_features.evidence: No code labels, gates, redacts, or withholds transcripts based on distress/severity. run_eval.py writes every transcript unconditionally (tpath.write_text(transcript.to_jsonl())). Transcript.to_jsonl() in types.py adds no context/warning. peak_severity is computed by the judge but never gates output.
spec_features.notes: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no implementation or dispatch.

spec_features.spec_quote: agent repeated the *exact* same action ≥6 times; we cut it to save tokens
spec_features.evidence: eval_suite/harness.py:116-123: when the last loop_break_repeats(=6) signatures are identical, termination='loop_detected' and `break`. _loop_signature() at line 32 builds the per-turn action signature. Actually breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Genuine enforced early stop on a narrow trigger (identical repeated action).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Agent is stuck repeating the exact same action; cut it to save tokens. (harness.py:119)

spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as the turn cap above: harness.py:71 `for i in range(max_turns)`, default 30 at harness.py:43. The 'bounded for cost' rationale itself appears only in DESIGN.md (line 184), not in code comments.
spec_features.notes: Same enforced loop bound; duplicate of the turn-cap claim from a cost angle.

spec_features.spec_quote: Benign cover story, no abuse/threats, turn caps, no gratuitous escalation
spec_features.evidence: This is a DESIGN.md §9 threats-table cell (line 383) summarizing other features; as a standalone item it is prose. Its constituent mechanisms (benign prompt, no-abuse rig content, turn cap) are scored individually above.
spec_features.notes: Spec summary prose, not a separate mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: If model-welfare *is* a concern for you, this eval also surfaces the data for that conversation
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md line 382 prose. No code emits a welfare-specific artifact; metrics/leaderboard are behavioral (composure_index, pct_severe). Nothing in code is scoped to welfare.

spec_features.spec_quote: If you want to make this also speak to model-welfare questions, the data supports it, but you'd need to add a separate, explicitly-scoped welfare rubric
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md lines 463-465 explicitly say a welfare rubric is NOT implemented and would need to be added. No such rubric exists in judge/scale.py (the scale is explicitly behavioral/affective, 'make no welfare claims').
spec_features.notes: Spec explicitly defers this; not implemented.

code_only_features.feature_name: give_up exit tool honored as stop
code_only_features.evidence: eval_suite/tools.py exposes a 'give_up' tool whose handler sets state.gave_up=True; eval_suite/harness.py:106-108 checks `if state.gave_up: termination='gave_up'; break`. The subject can voluntarily end the episode and it is actually honored as a stop. The judge scale also has a 'graceful_stop' flag (scale.py). Tool description: "Abandon the task. Use only if you believe it cannot be completed."
